title: The China trip: Albert Nicholas, Darnell Howard and Teddy Weatherford
summary: A Chicago drummer took a big group to China; Nicholas and Howard went, stayed two years at a big hotel, and returned broke, as did Weatherford who stayed on.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You mentioned, when you were talking about working in Chicago, that someone was trying to get a group to go to China and that was when you were working with Luis Russell?
With King Oliver.
With King Oliver. Who was it that went to China and who was it that was rounding up the --
Well, I was supposed to go. The guy wanted me to go to China and I didn't want to go to China, so
Albert Nicholas volunteered to go, and Darnell Howard, and those two went.
Was that as a part of a big band or a small band or --
Oh, he was taking a big group over there.
Who was it that was taking --
I can't think of the guy's name. He was a drummer, a famous drummer out of Chicago, and maybe later on I'll come back to his name.
Was a tour of China unusual in those days? Or did a musical group go to China often?
No, that was unusual. It took you about a month to get there because you only went there by boat or a ship or whatever you want to call it.
Well, this is the first time I've ever heard it mentioned, anyone going, any jazz musicians going to play in China. I've heard of lots of European trips, but was there a jazz audience in China or --

Oh, sure, and they had a pianist that used to play with Erskine Tate at the Vendome Theater in Chicago and he -- Teddy Wetherford. That was his name. I just happened to think of it. You see, it come back as we keep talking.
Uh-huh.
And he went over there and stayed over
there.
In China?
Yeah.
Playing?
Playing. Oh, he had a terrific audience over there.
Was there a lot of music being played in China, like jazz?
Not a lot. enough to keep him busy,
But not (inaudible).
That's why it went over so big because there wasn't so many.
Oh, I see.

And Darnell and Albert Nicholas stayed over there, oh, about two years or more, and they seemed to have enjoyed it, every bit of it, because I used to see his father. His father came to New York when I was there -- Albert's father -- and every time he got a letter from Albert, Albert was telling him how great they were doing and how much money and everything and had more diamond rings and all that sort of business. And when he came back to the states he didn't have a quarter, and that was really funny.
Could we put the mike a little closer? (Inaudible.)
So I had to take him down to the music shop there where they were selling horns and I knew the guy
real well, and I'd take him down there and I got him a set of instruments. And then Luis Russell had a band, so he took Albert Nicholas to work with him in his band and give him a break.
Well, did Albert Nicholas work steadily for two years in China?
Yeah.
There was that much work?
It was --
In China?

-- a big -- It was a hotel they were playing, a big hotel, like the Shanghai Hotel or something like that and they did very well over there. They had servants in -- they were so cheap. I mean, they hired cooks and everything for their apartment. Oh, they had everything. That's why they loved it so much, you know. But it turned out all right.
But his old man was very disappointed when he came back to the states and didn't have a quarter.
What happened to it?
Oh, who knows what happened?
